dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Commanders (4-5-1) Week 12 Briefing: Wednesday Injury Report Ahead of Cardinals
bullets: Bengals Offensive Surge: Fresh off moving to 4-5-1 (3rd in NFC East) with a 22–20 win over Cincinnati, Washington piled up 428 total yards [NFL Trade Rumors](https://nfltraderumors.co/nfc-notes-brandon-aiyuk-jayden-daniels-commanders-eagles-giants/) [Sanjesh Singh](https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/sports/nfl/commanders-bengals-score-joe-burrow-jayden-daniels/4187269/). Jacory Croskey-Merritt totaled 77 scrimmage yards and 1 touchdown while Jayden Daniels threw for 289 yards and 0 TDs in Dan Quinn's attack [John Keim](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50595281/brandon-aiyuk-finishes-visit-commanders).

Injury & Practice Status: WR Treylon Burks (foot) logged limited practice reps Wednesday [The Associated Press and Gina Cook](https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/sports/washington-commanders/commanders-wr-terry-mclaurin-out-for-the-season-after-knee-injury/4169719/). CB Amik Robertson (ankle) did not practice Wednesday, with Stefon Diggs taking veteran rest [Scott Bair](https://www.hogshaven.com/washington-commanders-injuries/457040/commanders-cardinals-wednesday-injury-report-amik-robertson-stefon-diggs).

Week 12 Cardinals Outlook: Dan Quinn and DC Daronte Jones open installation for the Arizona Cardinals (3-8, WSH -7, HC Mike LaFleur, OC Nathaniel Hackett & DC Nick Rallis (Road Test)) as Washington prepares for a pivotal NFC matchup [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/preview?gameId=401873092).

NFC Playoff Trajectory: Entering Week 12 at 4-5-1 (3rd in NFC East • #11 Seed in NFC), Washington carries a 15.2% postseason projection, 13.8% NFC East division title mark, and 0% #1 Seed Bye equity into the conference stretch [NFL Trade Rumors](https://nfltraderumors.co/nfc-notes-brandon-aiyuk-jayden-daniels-commanders-eagles-giants/).

Statistical Profile & Matchup Edge: Through Week 11, Washington ranks #19 in Points / Game (21.8), #20 in Points Allowed / Game (24.3), #3 in Turnover Differential (+7), giving Dan Quinn and Daronte Jones a clear benchmark ahead of Sun, Nov 29, 4:25 PM EST • NFL TV at [object Object] against the Arizona Cardinals [bill-in-bangkok](https://www.hogshaven.com/washington-commanders-news/457323/for-the-first-time-in-years-its-fun-to-watch-the-commanders-play-defense).

rawStream.fullText:
GM Adam Peters, during his paid weekly appearance with the @junksradio, on Brandon Aiyuk:

"One of the things that I don't think anyone can dispute is his work ethic. He was one of the hardest workers on the team. That's how he became an All-Pro type player... The last season I was there he had a fantastic season. He was a true No. 1 receiver at the time. He's a guy who's a tough cover, he's great after the catch. There's a lot of great things about him on the field and he worked really hard to get there. It wasn't just that he was the most gifted guy; he's self made too. There's a lot of positives. One thing that stands out to me is his work ethic."

Peters also called him a "smart football player." Said he hasn't talked to him since leaving. Also said there's a difference between being in shape and "football shape" so IF signed, will adjust expectations accordingly.
